blog_outline.title: The garage enclosure question: five shapes, what each costs you when the car comes back
blog_outline.audience: the garage builder who still parks
sections: Open with the number everyone meets first: a GSF builder found '$5,000 appeared to be the average price' and bought a $414 Walmart cage instead; another put a Carl's kit and $106 of EMT together for $1,006. The spread is the story.

Shape 1, the net cage (Net Return Pro $795, Spornia SPG-8 $499.99): 3.5 to 8 ft of depth, folds or pops down in minutes, no projection unless you add a target sheet; floor space when the car comes back: zero, it lives in a bag or against the wall.

Shape 2, the fixed frame (Carl's DIY from $999.95 plus pipe, GoSports $749.99 to $999.99, SIG8 $1,439.99, SIG10 $1,599.99, GolfBays SimBox $1,444.15, SwingBay $1,999, Carl's Pro from $3,409.95): 4 ft 2 in to 6 ft deep by 8 to 12 ft wide, permanently; the car does not come back to that bay. Frame heights 7 ft 7 in (SimStudio8) to 9 ft 4 in (SIG12) decide the ceiling.

Shape 3, the retractable (HomeCourse ProScreen 180 $1,999 to $2,299, SportScreen Vanish from $2,999.99, Vanish LITE from $2,299.99, G-TRAK from $1,999.99, DIY curtain track from $30 to $599): the bay rolls to the ceiling or the wall; needs 8 ft 6 in (HomeCourse) or a joist or a door rail; owners report wrinkles, bottom gap and install time; the garage keeps its parking.

Shape 4, the freestanding fold-flat: the DIY precedents (hinged Carl's panels to a 1 x 8 ft footprint in 2020; a frame on velcro straps pivoting into a 9 ft 6 in ceiling in 2017; a hoisted steel frame into cut trusses in 2023) and the products that claim a fold (Anything Sports wall-mounted $899.99 to $999.99, Impact Sports $2,338, StowGolf $2,495 list, first 25 at $2,295, 10 ft wide, 5 ft deep, 7 ft 6 in to the screen top, nothing drilled). Disclosure: Brett Martin runs Teed and builds StowGolf.

Shape 5, the inflatable and the custom room: All Sports 12 x 16 at $2,999 needs 12 x 16 ft of floor; a custom room is $50k to $100k (ForeFront) or $34,995-plus (Premier Sims) and the car never comes back.

The DIY math, sourced: Carl's kit $999.95 to $1,199.94 plus 9 to 12 EMT sticks at $8 to $12 (2026) or the $349.95 pipe kit; the $500 blueprint (11 sticks ~$250, foam $30, online-only fittings $65 to $279, a $100 to $300 screen); the Gung Ho 16 x 9 at ~$1,060; and the two forum totals, $1,006 and $1,263. What you do not get: padding, a baffle, a warranty, and a Saturday.

The 8-ft ceiling question, sourced: golfingsim.com's tier table (under 8 ft: wall-hung panel; 8 to 8 ft 6 in: a sub-8-ft frame, driver only under 5 ft 8 in; 9 ft: the standard 8 ft 4 in frame; 10 ft: Pro); the 2 to 3 in frame buffer and the 2 to 2.5 in a mat eats; the GSF 8 ft 4 in garage that moved the mat 9 ft from the screen and cleared driver; The Indoor Golf Shop's 'advise against under 9 ft'; the one product frame under 8 ft (SimStudio8 at 7 ft 6 in) and StowGolf's 7 ft 6 in to the screen top. No ranking; the reader measures to the lowest obstruction, not the drywall.

What 'folds' actually means across products, sourced claims only: Net Return and Spornia fold to a bag; GolfBays 'folds down for storage' with no folded dimension published; Elite GolfSim Portable has a folding frame and a carry bag (44 lb boxed); Anything Sports 'folds nearly flat in about a minute' against the wall it is bolted to; Impact Sports 'folds to 13 in width', mount unstated; HomeCourse, Vanish and G-TRAK retract rather than fold; StowGolf 'folds flat against the wall', freestanding. The DIY hinged build folds to about 1 x 8 ft.

Bounce-back is an enclosure problem, not a screen problem: the GSF fixes (loosen bungees, trim bars 1/2 to 3/4 in, foam behind the top half, 12 in baffles 16 in apart, a soft floor) apply to every shape above.
Close with the reference bag embed and the builder's three numbers: width x depth x ceiling as measured, driver yes or no, and the price paid with its date.
